title: B2 · L15 — Advanced articles
topic: Advanced use of a/an, the and zero article
description: Uso avanzado de artículos: cero, generic, geográfico e institucional. Puntos finos que distinguen a un B2 competente.

questions.prompt: Situación: escribes la primera línea de un ensayo filosófico.
questions.question: Complete: '___ life is full of surprises.'
questions.explanation: Con sustantivos ABSTRACTOS usados en sentido GENERAL (life, love, happiness, freedom, art, music) NO se usa artículo — es el 'artículo cero' o 'zero article'. Error clásico de hispanohablante: usar 'the' por calco de 'la vida', 'el amor'. Regla clave: si hablas del concepto en abstracto, sin artículo.
examples: Life is what happens while you're busy making other plans. → cita clásica de Lennon
Love is patient, love is kind — the famous line from the wedding reading.

questions.prompt: Comentas tus gustos musicales en una entrevista.
questions.question: Complete: 'I love ___ music, especially ___ music of the 1960s.'
questions.explanation: Regla dorada: 'music' general (todo lo que suena) → sin artículo; 'the music of the 1960s' específico y delimitado por 'of...' → 'the'. La presencia de un modificador restrictivo (of the 60s, in this album, from Brazil) convierte lo general en específico y activa 'the'.
examples: I like coffee, but I really hate the coffee they serve at this hotel. → gusto vs crítica
She studies history, especially the history of ancient Egypt. → interés académico

questions.statement: Decimos 'go to school' sin 'the' cuando significa 'ir a estudiar'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Las instituciones usadas para su PROPÓSITO PRINCIPAL van sin artículo: go to school (estudiar), go to church (rezar), go to bed (dormir), go to hospital (ser paciente, UK), go to prison (como recluso). Con 'the', se refieren al EDIFICIO físico como visitante ('I went to THE school to meet the teacher').
examples: The children are at school right now — they'll be home at 4. → propósito: estudiar
The parents went to the school last night for the parent-teacher meeting. → edificio como visitante

questions.text: The United States is a country that attracts people from all over the world.
questions.explanation: 'The' obligatorio con países plurales o con 'United/Republic/Kingdom' en su nombre: The United States, The Netherlands, The UK, The Czech Republic. Curiosidad: 'The United States IS' (singular) porque se percibe como una entidad única. Connected speech: 'from all over the world' se enlaza fluidamente. Prosodia clara y neutra.
examples: The Philippines is an incredibly beautiful country with over 7,000 islands. → dato geográfico
The Czech Republic has some of the most stunning Gothic architecture in Europe.

questions.prompt: Cuentas a un amigo un viaje reciente.
questions.question: Which is correct?
options: I visited the Mount Everest last year.
I visited Mount Everest last year.
I visited a Mount Everest last year.
I visited an Mount Everest last year.
questions.explanation: Nombres de MONTAÑAS INDIVIDUALES van SIN artículo: Mount Everest, Mount Fuji, Mount Kilimanjaro. Pero CORDILLERAS (grupos de montañas) llevan 'the': the Alps, the Himalayas, the Andes, the Rockies. Regla: singular sin artículo, plural con 'the'.
examples: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest peak on the entire African continent. → dato geográfico
The Andes stretch across seven countries in South America. → cordillera con 'the'

questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Ríos, océanos, mares, canales y golfos SIEMPRE llevan 'the': the Amazon, the Nile, the Thames, the Pacific, the Atlantic, the Mediterranean, the Panama Canal, the Gulf of Mexico. Regla mnemotécnica: si es agua con nombre propio, casi siempre 'the'. Excepciones: lagos individuales (Lake Victoria, sin 'the').
examples: The Thames flows right through the heart of London.
The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and the Pacific — one of the great feats of engineering.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada inicio con su continuación (artículo correcto):
questions.explanation: Reglas visibles: zero article con conceptos abstractos generales (art, music), ciudades y países individuales (New York, France); 'the' con museos, países compuestos/plurales (United Kingdom), océanos, ríos. Museos, hoteles, teatros y periódicos concretos casi siempre 'the'.
examples: I've been into Japanese food ever since my trip to Kyoto in 2018.
The Louvre is in the very heart of Paris — worth going even just for the building.

questions.prompt: Presentas a una amiga músico en un evento cultural.
questions.question: Complete: 'She plays ___ violin beautifully.'
questions.explanation: Con INSTRUMENTOS MUSICALES usados en general se usa 'the': play the piano, play the guitar, play the violin. CONTRASTE clave: con DEPORTES va sin artículo (play football, play tennis, play chess). Curiosidad: en inglés hablado moderno se oye a veces 'play piano' sin artículo, pero en escritura formal 'the' sigue siendo la norma.
examples: He plays the piano professionally at hotel lounges around Europe. → dato biográfico
She started playing the flute when she was just five years old.

questions.target: The elderly often struggle with new technology, but their wisdom is invaluable to society.
questions.explanation: 'The + adjetivo' se usa para referirse a GRUPOS SOCIALES como colectivo: the elderly, the poor, the rich, the unemployed, the homeless. Toma verbo en PLURAL (the elderly ARE, no IS). Prosodia: pausa reflexiva tras 'technology', énfasis en 'invaluable'. Registro típico de debate social o ensayo de opinión.
examples: The rich keep getting richer while the poor struggle to make ends meet. → editorial
The unemployed need much better support systems than what's currently in place.

questions.question: Complete: 'I read ___ newspaper every morning.'
questions.explanation: 'The newspaper' se entiende como el periódico que uno lee habitualmente (definido por contexto), o como el concepto general de 'prensa'. Otros ejemplos similares con 'the': the news, the radio, the TV, the cinema — cosas que se consumen como parte de la rutina cultural.
examples: She read about the scandal in the newspaper this morning over breakfast.
He watches the news every evening at 8 — hasn't missed it in 20 years. → hábito

questions.statement: 'A tiger is a dangerous animal' y 'Tigers are dangerous animals' expresan el mismo sentido genérico.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Para hablar de una especie o categoría EN GENERAL hay tres formas equivalentes: 'a/an + singular' (a tiger), 'plural sin artículo' (tigers), y 'the + singular' (the tiger — más formal/científico). Las tres funcionan; la elección depende del registro y del ritmo de la frase.
examples: A dog is a loyal pet. / Dogs are loyal pets. / The dog is a loyal companion. → tres formas equivalentes
An elephant has an excellent memory — they never forget a face. → registro divulgativo

questions.text: The Internet has completely transformed the way we communicate with each other.
questions.explanation: 'The Internet' SIEMPRE va con 'the' — se considera una entidad única e identificable (como 'the sun', 'the moon'). Contraste: 'Wi-Fi', 'email', 'social media' van SIN artículo. Prosodia formal, típica de artículo divulgativo. Connected speech: 'has completely' se enlaza suave, y 'each other' recibe énfasis social.
examples: The Internet is essential for modern life — hard to imagine going a day without it.
The world has genuinely changed because of the web, for better and for worse.

questions.prompt: Detecta el error en estas frases sobre países.
questions.question: Which sentence is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Países en SINGULAR sin 'United/Kingdom/Republic' NUNCA llevan artículo: France, Spain, Japan, China, Germany, Italy — todos sin 'the'. Este error es constante en hispanohablantes por calco de 'la Francia', 'el Japón'. Sí llevan 'the': países plurales (the Philippines, the Netherlands) o compuestos (the UK, the USA, the Czech Republic).
examples: Correct: I've been to Italy, Spain and Germany this year. → países sin 'the'
Correct: I've been to the UK, the USA and the Netherlands. → países con 'the'

questions.target: The homeless in this city deserve much more support than they currently receive from the government.
questions.explanation: 'The homeless' — grupo social como colectivo con verbo en plural. Prosodia: pausa entre 'currently receive' y 'from the government', énfasis moral en 'deserve much more'. Registro típico de artículo de opinión, editorial o debate político. Nativos añaden hedging: 'in my view', 'it's fair to say' para no sonar demasiado categóricos.
examples: The elderly in rural areas need much better access to healthcare — it's a genuine crisis.
The wealthy should pay their fair share of taxes instead of exploiting loopholes.

questions.prompt: Titular de noticias sobre un discurso presidencial.
questions.question: Complete: '___ Prime Minister will address ___ nation this evening.'
questions.explanation: 'The Prime Minister' — cargo único e identificable en el contexto (sólo hay uno en el país). 'The nation' — colectivo específico ('este país nuestro'). Ambos requieren 'the'. Regla clave: cargos únicos (the President, the CEO, the Pope) y colectivos identificables (the nation, the country, the government) llevan 'the'.
examples: The president will hold an urgent press conference at 8 p.m. tonight. → boletín informativo
The Queen traditionally addressed the nation on Christmas Day. → contexto histórico UK
